why: All three checks pass in the finding's favour. (1) The quoted sentence exists VERBATIM at settings.md:633 under "### Compute managed settings with a policy helper", and every element of the claimed behaviour is verbatim-supported in the same section: the key table (path / timeoutMs / refreshIntervalMs, "Set to 0 to disable refresh, or to at least 60000"), the envelope ("Put the settings under a managedSettings key rather than at the top level"), single-source precedence ("that object becomes the only managed settings source for the run"), and "When the helper exits non-zero at startup, Claude Code prints the error and refuses to start". (2) packages/shared/src/config/managed-composition.ts:29 says exactly what was claimed — ' * rather than merged", `policyHelper` > remote > MDM > file-based > HKCU.' — a docblock quoting Claude's precedence chain; binary-safe `grep -rna --binary-files=text "policyHelper" packages apps scripts` returns exactly one hit, that line. (3) One layer up, resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy (packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/managed-policy-resolution.ts:127) composes only two seams, `file` and `delivered` — no helper seam, no third source. One layer down, MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/managed-policy.ts:501) has no policyHelper and refuseUnknownKeys (:727) strips it as "invalid managed Pi policy key" — a visible drop, not an implementation. No sibling subsystem could have been misnamed: apiKeyHelper / headersHelper / awsAuthRefresh / credentialHelper return zero hits in packages/shared/src/config and packages/server-core/src, so no helper-executable mechanism exists anywhere to attribute it to. It is NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (I read all nine at :89-97). It is NOT a fork product difference: the doc honours policyHelper from MDM OR a system managed-settings.json, and we ship that second scope rebranded — managedPiPolicyPathForPlatform resolves /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json, %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json, read under a host-owned ownership/mode/symlink regime — so the eligible configuration scope exists in this fork.
correctedState:
Two corrections to the finding's framing, neither of which touches its substance.

FIRST, "exactly once repo-wide" is true only of shipped code. `policyHelper` appears once in packages/apps/scripts (managed-composition.ts:29) but in eight docs files besides. Precise statement: it appears exactly once in shipped source, inside a docblock quoting Claude's managed-tier precedence chain; it is absent from MANAGED_PI_POLICY_KEYS, from every seam of resolveEnforcedManagedPolicy, and from any spawn/parse/timer path. An admin who writes the key into our system managed-policy.json has it stripped by refuseUnknownKeys with the diagnostic "invalid managed Pi policy key: policyHelper" — reported, not silently ignored.

SECOND, the gap is already tracked, so this is a re-derivation rather than a new discovery, and the parent should file it against the existing row instead of opening one:
- docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-server-managed-delivery.md:212-216 declares it out of scope: "Per-group configuration (:127 …), `policyHelper` and `wslInheritsWindowsSettings` (:129 — OS-policy sources only)". Echoed at docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-delivered-policy-enforcement.md:245.
- docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-deviation-audit.md:193 carries it as an R25b row inside §2 "Unjustified divergences, ordered by parity distance", Tier 3, with action "Record as C" and cost "~ record". Category C in that audit's legend (:59) is "documented, not implemented" — a tracked open item, NOT a closed owner decision.
- docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:474 struck a policyHelper candidate from Step 3's twenty as one of "four already owned … would have been duplicates", naming the R25b line as its owner. (That bullet's opening line was lost in a later edit and now dangles; the intact text is in commit 666c2fdf.)

The recorded reason is HALF-COVERING and should not be read as closing the gap. "OS-policy sources only, per server-managed-settings.md:129" correctly excludes policyHelper from the server-delivered channel — settings.md:633 agrees that Claude ignores it in server-managed settings — but it does not justify absence from the system-FILE loader, which is the other scope the same sentence names as valid ("Configure it from MDM or a system managed-settings.json file") and which this fork does ship at /Library/Application Support/Nessy/managed-policy.json, /etc/nessy/managed-policy.json and %ProgramData%\Nessy\managed-policy.json. So the correct disposition is: real C-category gap, already owned by R25b, with the existing justification covering only the delivered channel and the file-scope half still unjustified.
